title: Torre dei Conti
authoredRepresentation: Intact pre-collapse exterior documented in the 2012 study and 2013/2024 photographs; historical only, valid before 3 November 2025
currentStateResearchTarget: Surviving exterior after the 2025 collapse and the 2026 stabilization, with an explicit observation date

establishedFacts.fact: The collapse on 3 November 2025 removed the central southern buttress and part of the sloping base. A second collapse affected the stair and roof slab.
The fire service handed the stabilized structure back to Rome on 28 April 2026. Work included wall reinforcement, internal steel bracing, beams and a final roof covering.

Official April photographs show the missing buttress scar, temporary roof overhang, braced openings and surviving corner buttresses. A ceremonial flag and fire-service vehicles obscure portions of the facade.

Paola Porretta's primary architectural study reproduces measured plans supplied by Rome's heritage authority, including the surviving medieval core and later buttresses. Printed pages 82–83 are plans of the pre-collapse structure. Historical restoration proposals on earlier pages were not built and cannot be treated as current geometry.

mapEvidence.limitations: The overall mapped envelope is registered to the published restored west facade, toward Via dei Fori Imperiali. It does not resolve the current damaged southern wall.

remainingWork: Resolve the complete exposed southern wall, sloping base and roof silhouette from dated current exterior photographs or conservation elevations.
Author the observed damaged/stabilized exterior and retain its observation date; do not silently restore the missing buttress or historical upper stories.
Render all sides, verify current materials and placement, and bind reviews to source/runtime/frame hashes.
decision: Retain the original candidate identity. A dated original source GLB has been created and awaits visual review. Its historical-proposal status and currentWorldEligible:false prevent it from being placed as an intact current landmark. No substitute identity or maximum-fidelity approval is claimed.
